text: In a small village on the edge of rolling green hills, a young shepherd boy looked after a large flock of fluffy white sheep every day. His job was to keep them safe from wolves while the village farmers worked the fields below.

Day after day, nothing exciting ever happened. The boy grew terribly bored watching the sheep munch grass. "I know how to have some fun!" he said with a mischievous grin.

He cupped his hands and screamed: "WOLF! WOLF! There's a wolf attacking the sheep!"

The farmers dropped their tools and came racing up the hill, panting and worried. But when they arrived, there was no wolf — just the boy laughing hysterically.

"Ha ha ha! I was just joking!" The farmers shook their heads and went back to work, grumbling.

The next week, bored again, the boy cried wolf a second time. "WOLF! WOLF! Help! It's real this time!"

Again the farmers ran up the hill. Again there was no wolf. This time they were much angrier. "Stop lying!" they warned. "We won't come again!"

Then one grey afternoon, a REAL wolf crept out of the dark forest, his yellow eyes gleaming. He snarled and lunged at the flock! The terrified boy screamed at the top of his lungs.

"WOLF! WOLF! PLEASE HELP ME! IT'S REAL! IT'S REAL!"

But the farmers heard him and said, "That boy is lying again." No one came. The wolf scattered the sheep across the hills, and the boy sat alone on the hillside, crying real tears.

That evening, the village elder sat beside him and said softly, "Now you understand."

"Nobody believes a liar, even when they tell the truth," said the elder gently. "Honesty is the most important gift you can give to others — and to yourself."

The boy never lied again.

🌟 THE END 🌟

💡 Moral: Always tell the truth. A liar is never believed!
